title.zh: 卷431 列傳二百十八 郭松林 李长乐 杨鼎勋 唐殿魁 唐定奎 滕嗣武 骆国忠
title.en: Volume 431 Biographies 218: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, Tang Diankui, Tang Dingkui, Teng Siwu, Luo Guozhong
title.raw: 卷431 列傳二百十八 郭松林 李长乐 杨鼎勋 唐殿魁 唐定奎 滕嗣武 骆国忠

sentences.zh: 列傳二百十八

translations.literal: Biographies 218
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 218

sentences.zh: 郭松林李長樂楊鼎勳唐殿魁唐定奎

translations.literal: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, Tang Diankui, Tang Dingkui
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, Tang Diankui, and Tang Dingkui

sentences.zh: 滕嗣武駱國忠

translations.literal: Teng Siwu, Luo Guozhong
translations.idiomatic: Teng Siwu and Luo Guozhong

sentences.zh: 郭松林，字子美，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Guo Songlin, courtesy name Zimei, was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songlin, styled Zimei, came from Xiangtan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，隸曾國荃軍，從援江西，克安福，從剿永新、太和、萬安、蓮花廳、龍泉，敘獎把總。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he was attached to Zeng Guoquan's army, followed in the relief of Jiangxi, captured Anfu, and joined in suppressing Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua Department, and Longquan, and was rewarded with the rank of dartai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he joined Zeng Guoquan's forces, marched to relieve Jiangxi, took Anfu, and helped pacify Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua, and Longquan, for which he received the rank of dartai.

sentences.zh: 進圍吉安府城，七年，石達開率悍黨來援，邀擊於吉水三曲灘，松林首陷陣，多斬獲，收復新喻、峽江、吉水。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Ji'an Prefecture city, in the seventh year Shi Dakai led fierce partisans to relieve it; they were intercepted at Sanqu Beach in Jishui; Songlin was first to break the enemy line, with many beheadings and captures, and recovered Xinyu, Xiajiang, and Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: When the army pressed the siege of Ji'an, in 1857 Shi Dakai brought a fierce relief force; Songlin led the attack at Sanqu Beach on the Jishui River, was first into the enemy ranks, won heavy kills and captures, and recovered Xinyu, Xiajiang, and Jishui.

sentences.zh: 八年，隨克吉安，擢守備。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed in the capture of Ji'an and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he took part in the fall of Ji'an and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，克景德、浮梁，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jingde and Fuliang were captured, and he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he helped capture Jingde and Fuliang and was awarded the peacock-feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 十年，圍安慶，會剿陳玉成於小池驛，進壁集賢關，每戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Anqing was besieged; he joined in suppressing Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi Post, advanced and fortified at Jixian Pass, and every battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he joined the siege of Anqing, fought Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi Post, pushed forward to hold Jixian Pass, and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，擢游擊，賜號奮勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was captured; he was promoted to battalion commander and granted the title Brave Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Anqing fell; he was made battalion commander and given the honorific title Fenyong Baturu ("Valiant Baturu").

sentences.zh: 克廬江、無為、運漕鎮，下沿江要隘，擢參將。

translations.literal: Lujiang, Wuwei, and Yuncao Town were captured, and key passes along the river were taken; he was promoted to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Lujiang, Wuwei, and Yuncao Town and seize the vital Yangtze strongpoints, and was promoted to brigade general.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章率淮軍八千赴上海，松林從，與偽忠王李秀成偽慕王譚紹光大戰滬西，破賊眾十萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army troops to Shanghai; Songlin followed, and with the rebel Loyal King Li Xiucheng and the rebel Admiring King Tan Shaoguang fought a great battle west of Shanghai, breaking one hundred thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army men to Shanghai; Songlin went with him and, facing the Taiping Loyal King Li Xiucheng and Admiring King Tan Shaoguang, fought a major battle west of the city and routed a rebel host of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 會攻太倉，砲擊城隳，士卒爭進，浮橋斷，賊乘之，死數百人，松林力禦，始得收軍。

translations.literal: In the joint attack on Taicang, cannon fire breached the wall; soldiers rushed forward, the pontoon bridge broke, and rebels took advantage; several hundred died; Songlin fought hard to hold them off before the army could withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Taicang, artillery smashed the wall and troops rushed the breach; the pontoon bridge gave way and rebels surged in, killing several hundred men before Songlin fought them off and pulled the force back.

sentences.zh: 二年，克太倉，松林敗賊茜涇、支塘，會克崑山、新陽，以總兵用。

translations.literal: In the second year Taicang was captured; Songlin defeated rebels at Qianjing and Zhitang, and jointly captured Kunshan and Xinyang; he was employed with the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Taicang fell; Songlin routed rebels at Qianjing and Zhitang and helped take Kunshan and Xinyang, and was appointed acting regional commander.

sentences.zh: 李秀成合水陸數十萬援江陰，犯常熟，劉銘傳謀乘賊未定擊之。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng combined several hundred thousand land and water forces to relieve Jiangyin and attacked Changshu; Liu Mingchuan planned to strike while the rebels were not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng mustered several hundred thousand men by land and water to relieve Jiangyin and threatened Changshu; Liu Mingchuan proposed striking before the rebels could dig in.

sentences.zh: 賊北自北漍，南至張涇橋，東自陳市，西至長壽，縱橫六七十里，築壘憑河，勢大熾。

translations.literal: The rebels extended from Beigang in the north to Zhangjing Bridge in the south, from Chenshi in the east to Changshou in the west, sixty or seventy li across, building fortifications along the rivers; their power grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stretched from Beigang in the north to Zhangjing Bridge in the south and from Chenshi in the east to Changshou in the west—sixty or seventy li of entrenchments along the waterways—and their position looked formidable.

sentences.zh: 銘傳進北漍攻其左，松林進南漍攻其右，周盛波等進麥市橋為中路，黃翼升以水師助之。

translations.literal: Mingchuan advanced from Beigang to attack their left; Songlin advanced from Nangang to attack their right; Zhou Shengbo and others advanced on Maishi Bridge as the center; Huang Yisheng assisted with the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan attacked from Beigang on the left, Songlin from Nangang on the right, Zhou Shengbo and others up the center at Maishi Bridge, and Huang Yisheng's fleet supported from the water.

sentences.zh: 松林敗賊陳市，越南漍趨張涇，揮刀盪決，血染衣盡赤，賊大潰走。

translations.literal: Songlin defeated the rebels at Chenshi, crossed south of Nangang toward Zhangjing, wielded his blade to cut through, blood staining his clothes entirely red; the rebels fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Songlin routed the rebels at Chenshi, crossed south of Nangang toward Zhangjing, and hacked his way through until his clothes were soaked red with blood; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 銘傳、盛波等同破賊，自顧山以西皆盡，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Mingchuan, Shengbo, and others jointly broke the rebels; from Gushan westward all were cleared; he was recorded with the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan, Shengbo, and the rest drove the rebels out until everything west of Gushan was cleared, and Songlin was entered on the rolls as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 尋克江陰，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiangyin was captured, and he was recorded with the rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin fell soon after, and he was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 又破賊緱山、梅村、麻塘橋，松林受矛傷，既而蘇州、無錫皆复，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Goushan, Meicun, and Matang Bridge; Songlin received a spear wound; soon Suzhou and Wuxi were both recovered, and he was granted the first-rank official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed the rebels at Goushan, Meicun, and Matang Bridge; Songlin was wounded by a spear, but Suzhou and Wuxi were soon recovered, and he received the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 三年，克宜興、荊溪，敗賊張渚，毀賊壘，收溧陽，解常熟圍，授福山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the third year Yixing and Jingxi were captured, rebels were defeated at Zhangzhu, rebel fortifications were destroyed, Liyang was taken, the siege of Changshu was lifted, and he was appointed regional commander of Fushan Town.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he took Yixing and Jingxi, defeated the rebels at Zhangzhu, destroyed their fortifications, recovered Liyang, and lifted the siege of Changshu, and was made regional commander at Fushan Town.

sentences.zh: 大破三河口賊營，賊爭道，六浮橋盡斷，屍塞河，水為不流。

translations.literal: The rebel camp at Sanhekou was greatly broken; rebels scrambled for the road; six pontoon bridges were all cut; corpses blocked the river so the water would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed the rebel camp at Sanhekou; as the enemy fled in a crush, six pontoon bridges collapsed under them and corpses choked the river until the water barely moved.

sentences.zh: 克常州，進剿浙西，克長興，复湖州，功皆最。

translations.literal: Changzhou was captured; he advanced to suppress western Zhejiang, captured Changxing, and recovered Huzhou; in each his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou fell; he pushed into western Zhejiang, took Changxing, and recovered Huzhou, ranking first in merit in each action.

sentences.zh: 賊走廣德、徽州，合江寧、杭州賊自江西竄閩。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Guangde and Huizhou; those of Jiangning and Hangzhou combined with rebels from Jiangxi and fled into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels retreated toward Guangde and Huizhou, while survivors from Nanjing and Hangzhou joined forces with rebels driven from Jiangxi and slipped into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 四年，李鴻章檄松林率五千人航海赴援，克漳州、漳浦、雲霄、詔安，賊竄廣東嘉應，遂破滅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Li Hongzhang ordered Songlin to lead five thousand men by sea to relieve Fujian; Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, Yunxiao, and Zhao'an were captured; the rebels fled to Jiaying in Guangdong and were there destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 Li Hongzhang ordered Songlin to sail south with five thousand men; they took Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, Yunxiao, and Zhao'an, and the rebels who fled into Jiaying, Guangdong, were finally wiped out.

sentences.zh: 五年，曾國荃調松林率新募湘軍剿捻匪於德安，克應城、雲夢，复敗之皁河、楊澤。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Zeng Guoquan transferred Songlin to lead newly recruited Xiang Army troops to suppress Nian bandits at De'an; Yingcheng and Yunmeng were captured, and they were again defeated at Zaohe and Yangze.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 Zeng Guoquan sent Songlin with freshly raised Xiang troops to fight the Nian in De'an; they took Yingcheng and Yunmeng and again defeated the bandits at Zaohe and Yangze.

sentences.zh: 追至臼口，中伏，松林傷足，臥地不能起。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Jiukou, they fell into an ambush; Songlin was wounded in the foot and lay on the ground unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuit carried them to Jiukou, where they walked into an ambush; Songlin was shot in the foot and could not get up.

sentences.zh: 將卒不見松林，复闖入陣，負而出之。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers, not seeing Songlin, again charged into the formation and carried him out on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: When his men could not find him, they charged back into the fight and carried him out.

sentences.zh: 弟芳珍戰死。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fangzhen died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fangzhen was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 松林以創重假歸。

translations.literal: Songlin, because his wounds were severe, took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Songlin went home on leave to recover from his serious wounds.

sentences.zh: 六年，創愈，李鴻章令統萬人號武毅軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his wounds healed; Li Hongzhang ordered him to command ten thousand men called the Wuyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867, once he had healed, Li Hongzhang put him in command of ten thousand men under the name Wuyi Army ("Army of Martial Resolution").

sentences.zh: 時東捻任柱已斃，餘黨走壽光，松林要擊，破之杞城。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern Nian leader Ren Zhu was already dead; the remnant party fled to Shouguang; Songlin intercepted them and broke them at Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: By then the eastern Nian leader Ren Zhu was dead and the survivors were heading for Shouguang; Songlin intercepted them and crushed them at Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 賊沿海南走，阻瀰河，捻酋牛喜子麾白旗賊犯劉銘傳軍；

translations.literal: The rebels fled south along the coast, blocked at the Mi River; the Nian chief Niu Xizi led White Banner rebels to attack Liu Mingchuan's army;
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled south along the coast until they were stopped at the Mi River; the Nian chief Niu Xizi led the White Banner force against Liu Mingchuan;

sentences.zh: 賴文光麾藍旗賊犯松林軍。

translations.literal: Lai Wenguang led Blue Banner rebels to attack Songlin's army.
translations.idiomatic: while Lai Wenguang led the Blue Banner against Songlin.

sentences.zh: 兩軍縱擊，賊大潰，壽光民圩皆出助殺，賊赴瀰河死，浮屍二萬餘，俘萬餘人，奪獲騾馬二萬匹。

translations.literal: Both armies charged freely; the rebels fled in great rout; Shouguang civilian stockades all came out to help kill; rebels rushed into the Mi River and died; more than twenty thousand corpses floated; more than ten thousand were captured; twenty thousand mules and horses were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Both columns pressed the attack and the bandits broke; militia from the Shouguang stockades joined the slaughter, and thousands drowned in the Mi River—over twenty thousand bodies floated on the water, more than ten thousand were taken alive, and twenty thousand pack animals were captured.

sentences.zh: 賊酋徐昌先、范汝增、任定皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The rebel chiefs Xu Changxian, Fan Ruzeng, and Ren Ding were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leaders Xu Changxian, Fan Ruzeng, and Ren Ding were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 賴文光鳧水南奔，松林疾馳六百里，追至清江。

translations.literal: Lai Wenguang fled south across the water; Songlin galloped six hundred li in pursuit to Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Wenguang swam south to escape; Songlin raced six hundred li in pursuit as far as Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 文光死奔，至揚州瓦窯鋪，為吳毓蘭所擒。

translations.literal: Wenguang fled for his life to Wayao Post in Yangzhou and was captured by Wu Yulan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenguang fled for his life to Wayao Post near Yangzhou, where Wu Yulan captured him.

sentences.zh: 東捻平。

translations.literal: The eastern Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Nian rebellion was ended.

sentences.zh: 七年春，西捻犯畿輔，松林敗之安平，再破之茌平。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year the western Nian invaded the capital region; Songlin defeated them at Anping and again at Chiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1868 the western Nian raided the capital districts; Songlin defeated them at Anping and again at Chiping.

sentences.zh: 自臨邑築長圍至馬頰河，松林偕潘鼎新、王心安守之，敗賊於海豐，追至德州，歷十六晝夜，斬捕過半。

translations.literal: From Linyi a long encirclement was built to the Majia River; Songlin together with Pan Dingxin and Wang Xin'an guarded it, defeated rebels at Haifeng, pursued to Dezhou, through sixteen days and nights, beheading and capturing more than half.
translations.idiomatic: A cordon was thrown from Linyi to the Majia River, which Songlin held with Pan Dingxin and Wang Xin'an; they routed the bandits at Haifeng and chased them to Dezhou in sixteen days and nights of pursuit, killing or capturing more than half the force.

sentences.zh: 六月，松林會潘鼎新大破之沙河，俘斬四千。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Songlin joined Pan Dingxin in a great defeat at Shahe; four thousand were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In June he and Pan Dingxin inflicted a crushing defeat at Shahe, killing or capturing four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 捻走黃、運、徒駭河間，松林與銘傳縱橫要擊，張總愚赴水死。

translations.literal: The Nian fled among the Yellow, Grand Canal, and Tuhai rivers; Songlin and Mingchuan struck across their path; Zhang Zongyu rushed into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian fled among the Yellow, Grand Canal, and Tuhai rivers; Songlin and Mingchuan cut them off wherever they turned, until Zhang Zongyu drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，賜黃馬褂，予輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: The western Nian were pacified; he was granted the yellow riding jacket and given the hereditary office of Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: With the western Nian suppressed, he received the yellow riding jacket and a hereditary Commandant of Light Chariots title.

sentences.zh: 授湖北提督，調直隸。

translations.literal: He was appointed provincial military commander of Hubei and transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed provincial commander of Hubei and then transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，卒於官，優恤，建專祠，諡武壯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he died in office; generous condolence was granted, a special shrine was built, and the posthumous title Wuzhuang was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1880; the court granted generous mourning honors, built him a dedicated shrine, and gave him the posthumous name Wuzhuang ("Martial and Robust").

sentences.zh: 李長樂，字漢春，安徽盱眙人。

translations.literal: Li Changle, courtesy name Hanchun, was a native of Xuyi in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changle, styled Hanchun, came from Xuyi in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以外委從郭松林隸淮軍，充營官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, as an external deputy he followed Guo Songlin into the Huai Army and served as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, serving as an external deputy, he followed Guo Songlin into the Huai Army as battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 克柘林、奉賢、南匯、川沙、金山，解松江圍，复青浦，擢千總。

translations.literal: Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan were captured; the siege of Songjiang was lifted and Qingpu recovered; he was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan, lifted the siege of Songjiang, and recovered Qingpu, and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 戰四江口，松林軍方泰鎮，長樂率所部深入，近賊壘。

translations.literal: Fighting at Sijiangkou, Songlin's army was at Fangtai Town; Changle led his unit deep in, close to the rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Sijiangkou, while Songlin's main force was at Fangtai, Changle led his men deep behind the lines, almost on top of the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 夜半，趣軍士起，曰：「今陷賊中，旦明賊覺，無得脫者。

translations.literal: At midnight he urged the soldiers to rise and said: "We are now trapped among the rebels; at dawn when they discover us, none will escape.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he roused his men and said, "We are trapped in the middle of the enemy camp; at daybreak they will find us and none of us will get out.

sentences.zh: 盍出奇計劫之！

translations.literal: Why not use a surprise stratagem to raid them!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not strike first with a surprise raid?

sentences.zh: 」遂投火賊幕，鼓角乘之，賊驚擾，長樂奮呼進，大破之。

translations.literal: He then cast fire into the rebel camp, followed with drums and horns; the rebels were startled and thrown into disorder; Changle charged forward with a fierce shout and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He set fire to the rebel tents, sounded drums and horns, and as the enemy panicked he charged with a war cry and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 又設伏黃渡，擊之半濟，又敗之吳淞江南。

translations.literal: He again set an ambush at Huangdu, struck them mid-crossing, and again defeated them south of the Wusong River.
translations.idiomatic: He ambushed them at Huangdu while they were crossing the river, and defeated them again south of the Wusong.

sentences.zh: 四江口圍解，擢都司，賜花翎。

translations.literal: The siege at Sijiangkou was lifted; he was promoted to battalion commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The siege at Sijiangkou was lifted; he was promoted to battalion commander and awarded the peacock-feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 二年，進屯常熟王莊，援賊踞陳市，阻官軍進路。

translations.literal: In the second year he advanced and encamped at Wangzhuang in Changshu; relieving rebels held Chenshi and blocked the government army's advance.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he advanced to Wangzhuang near Changshu, where relieving rebels held Chenshi and blocked the government advance.

sentences.zh: 從松林自南漍攻賊右，連破賊營，直趨長涇。

translations.literal: Following Songlin he attacked the rebel right from Nangang, successively broke rebel camps, and pressed straight to Changjing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Songlin's attack on the rebel right from Nangang, stormed camp after camp, and drove straight for Changjing.

sentences.zh: 長樂陷陣傷脛，裹創力戰敗賊，擢參將，賜號侃勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Changle was first into the line and wounded in the shin; wrapping his wound he fought hard and defeated the rebels; he was promoted to brigade general and granted the title Kan'yong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: Changle led the charge and was wounded in the leg; he bound the wound and kept fighting until the rebels broke; he was made brigade general and given the title Kan'yong Baturu ("Outspoken and Brave Baturu").

sentences.zh: 尋克江陰，規無錫，出新塘橋。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiangyin was captured; he planned for Wuxi and came out at Xintang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin fell soon after; he turned toward Wuxi and advanced from Xintang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊憑壘鳴砲俯擊，長樂濡絮裹身越溝進，敗之；

translations.literal: The rebels relied on their fortifications and fired cannon downward; Changle soaked cotton padding and wrapped his body to cross the ditch and advance, and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shelled from their ramparts; Changle wrapped himself in wet cotton padding, crossed the ditch under fire, and routed them;

sentences.zh: 逐奔至亭子橋，刺賊酋黃子隆中肩，又設伏兵敗援賊。

translations.literal: pursued the rout to Tingzi Bridge, stabbed the rebel chief Huang Zilong in the shoulder, and again set ambush troops to defeat relieving rebels.
translations.idiomatic: pursued them to Tingzi Bridge, stabbed the rebel chief Huang Zilong in the shoulder, and ambushed and defeated the relief column.

sentences.zh: 李秀成圍大橋角營，從松林往援，奪其舟，賊退走，盡平梅村諸壘。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng besieged the Daqiaojiao camp; Changle followed Songlin to relieve it, seized their boats, the rebels retreated, and all fortifications at Meicun were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiucheng besieged the Daqiaojiao camp, Changle went with Songlin to relieve it, seized the rebel boats, drove them off, and cleared every fort around Meicun.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍圍攻無錫，率輕騎掩至，梯城入，黃子隆就擒，長樂獲其子德懋。

translations.literal: When the allied armies besieged Wuxi, he led light cavalry in a surprise approach, scaled the wall and entered; Huang Zilong was captured, and Changle took his son Demao.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Wuxi he led light cavalry in a surprise assault, scaled the walls, captured Huang Zilong, and took his son Demao prisoner.

sentences.zh: 尋坐失察部勇，褫職留軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for failure to supervise his troops, his office was stripped but he remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of rank for lax discipline among his troops but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 進規常州，援總兵唐殿魁於奔牛，解其圍。

translations.literal: Advancing to plan for Changzhou, he relieved regional commander Tang Diankui at Benniu and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: As the army moved on Changzhou, he relieved regional commander Tang Diankui at Benniu and broke the siege there.

sentences.zh: 三年，敗賊上湖橋，克宜興，复官。

translations.literal: In the third year he defeated rebels at Shanghu Bridge, captured Yixing, and was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he defeated the rebels at Shanghu Bridge, took Yixing, and had his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 移軍溧陽、金壇，戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He moved his army to Liyang and Jintan; every battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted operations to Liyang and Jintan and won every engagement there.

sentences.zh: 回援常熟，解其圍，連破賊於楊舍、華墅、周莊、三河口，會攻常州。

translations.literal: Returning to relieve Changshu, he lifted the siege and successively defeated rebels at Yangshe, Huashu, Zhouzhuang, and Sanhekou, and joined in the attack on Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to relieve Changshu, lifted the siege, and routed the rebels at Yangshe, Huashu, Zhouzhuang, and Sanhekou before joining the assault on Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，合圍，長樂先登，賊酋陳坤書、黃和錦就擒，復常州，擢副將，賜號尚勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the encirclement closed; Changle was first to scale the wall; rebel chiefs Chen Kunshu and Huang Hejin were captured; Changzhou was recovered; he was promoted to deputy regional commander and granted the title Shangyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In April, as the encirclement closed, Changle was first over the wall; the rebel chiefs Chen Kunshu and Huang Hejin were taken, Changzhou was recovered, and he was made deputy regional commander with the title Shangyong Baturu ("Esteemed and Brave Baturu").

sentences.zh: 從松林進克浙江長興，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Following Songlin he advanced and captured Changxing in Zhejiang; he was recorded with the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Songlin into Zhejiang and helped take Changxing, and was entered on the rolls as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 進湖州，破呂山賊。

translations.literal: Advancing on Huzhou, he defeated rebels at Lüshan.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on Huzhou, he routed the rebels at Lüshan.

sentences.zh: 攻賊酋黃文金於尹隆橋，官軍不利，長樂率三營別屯李家港，保糧道。

translations.literal: Attacking the rebel chief Huang Wenjin at Yinlong Bridge, the government army fared poorly; Changle led three battalions to encamp separately at Lijiagang to protect the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: An attack on the rebel chief Huang Wenjin at Yinlong Bridge went badly; Changle took three battalions to hold Lijiagang and keep the supply line open.

sentences.zh: 賊傾巢來爭，長樂偕易用剛夾擊之，斬賊酋黃十四，破尹隆橋，遂復湖州。

translations.literal: The rebels came out in full force to contest it; Changle together with Yi Yonggang struck them from both sides, beheaded the rebel chief Huang Fourteen, broke Yinlong Bridge, and thus recovered Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels threw their full strength at the position, Changle and Yi Yonggang caught them in a pincer, killed the rebel chief Huang Fourteen, broke through at Yinlong Bridge, and recovered Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年春，從松林援福建，戰於海澄赤嶺。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he followed Songlin to relieve Fujian and fought at Chiling in Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1865 he sailed with Songlin to Fujian and fought at Chiling near Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 松林分兵為八隊，長樂居中當賊首李世賢，破走之，竄漳州。

translations.literal: Songlin divided his forces into eight columns; Changle held the center against the rebel chief Li Shixian, broke and drove him off, and he fled to Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Songlin split his force into eight columns; Changle took the center against the rebel chief Li Shixian, routed him, and drove him toward Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長樂進屯古田，據山東形勝，賊悉銳力爭，擊卻之，复漳浦、雲霄。

translations.literal: Changle advanced and encamped at Gutian, holding the strategic terrain east of the mountains; the rebels brought all their elite strength to contest it; he struck and repelled them and recovered Zhangpu and Yunxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Changle pushed into Gutian and held the high ground east of the mountains; when the rebels threw their best troops at him he beat them back and recovered Zhangpu and Yunxiao.

sentences.zh: 南趨詔安，破之梅村，復其城，加提督銜。

translations.literal: He pressed south toward Zhao'an, defeated them at Meicun, recovered the city, and was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south to Zhao'an, defeated the rebels at Meicun, retook the city, and received brevet provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 福建平，旋師江蘇，屯鎮江。

translations.literal: Fujian was pacified; the army turned back to Jiangsu and encamped at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Fujian pacified, the force returned to Jiangsu and encamped at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓督師剿捻匪，松林已歸，長樂代將其眾以從，兼統忠樸三營，為游擊之師，轉戰河南、山東間。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan directed the campaign against Nian bandits; Songlin had already returned home; Changle took command of his troops and followed, also commanding the three battalions of Zhongpu, serving as a mobile strike force fighting between Henan and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan took command against the Nian, Songlin had already gone home and Changle led his old troops in the field, also taking the three Zhongpu battalions as a mobile strike force across Henan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 六年，李鴻章代國籓督師，松林復至軍，增松林軍至二十餘營，號武毅軍，長樂所部曰武毅軍前軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Li Hongzhang replaced Guofan in command; Songlin returned to the army; Songlin's force was increased to more than twenty battalions called the Wuyi Army; Changle's unit was called the Wuyi Army vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 Li Hongzhang replaced Guofan as commander; Songlin rejoined the campaign and expanded his command to more than twenty battalions under the name Wuyi Army, with Changle's unit as the Wuyi vanguard.

sentences.zh: 破任柱於贛榆，要賴文光於濰縣，長樂等並力奮擊，賊鳧水東走，躡至餘家寨，賊受創甚鉅，复要之壽光南北洋河、巨瀰河間，擒斬三萬，文光竄揚州被擒，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Ren Zhu was defeated at Ganyu; Lai Wenguang was intercepted at Weixian; Changle and others joined in a fierce attack; the rebels fled east across the water; pursuit reached Yujiazhai; the rebels suffered very heavy wounds; they were again intercepted between the North and South Yang Rivers and the great Mi River at Shouguang; thirty thousand were captured and beheaded; Wenguang fled to Yangzhou and was captured; the yellow riding jacket was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They broke Ren Zhu at Ganyu and caught Lai Wenguang at Weixian; Changle and the others pressed the attack until the bandits swam east in flight; pursuit reached Yujiazhai and then cut them off between the Yang Rivers and the great Mi River at Shouguang, killing or capturing thirty thousand; Wenguang fled to Yangzhou and was taken, and Changle received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 七年，從剿西捻，戰安平，馬軍失利，長樂等以步卒馳援，賊大潰；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in suppressing the western Nian; at Anping the cavalry fared poorly; Changle and others rushed infantry to relieve them; the rebels fled in great rout;
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he joined the campaign against the western Nian; at Anping, when the cavalry faltered, Changle rushed infantry to their aid and the bandits broke completely;

sentences.zh: 追至饒陽楊家村，又要之深州李家村，破其馬隊，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: pursuit reached Yangjia Village in Raoyang, and they were again intercepted at Lijia Village in Shenzhou; the rebel cavalry was broken; beheadings and captures were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: pursuit carried to Yangjia Village in Raoyang and another ambush at Lijia Village in Shenzhou shattered the rebel horse troops, with kills and captures beyond count.

sentences.zh: 三月，敗賊大坯山。

translations.literal: In the third month rebels were defeated at Dapishan.
translations.idiomatic: In March he defeated the bandits at Dapishan.

sentences.zh: 援提督陳振邦於大河村，解其圍，追挫之茌平、滄州，援副都統春壽於海豐郝家寨。

translations.literal: He relieved provincial commander Chen Zhenbang at Dahecun and lifted the siege; pursuit struck them at Chiping and Cangzhou; he relieved vice commander-in-chief Chun Shou at Haojiazhai in Haifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved provincial commander Chen Zhenbang at Dahecun, chased the bandits back at Chiping and Cangzhou, and rescued vice commander-in-chief Chun Shou at Haojiazhai in Haifeng.

sentences.zh: 六月，追至樂陵，擒總愚子正江、弟得華，戰商河，槍傷總愚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month pursuit reached Leling; Zongyu's son Zhengjiang and younger brother Dehua were captured; at Shanghe he fought and shot Zongyu with a musket.
translations.idiomatic: In June the pursuit reached Leling, where Zongyu's son Zhengjiang and brother Dehua were captured; at Shanghe Changle wounded Zongyu with a musket.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，以提督總兵遇缺題奏，晉博奇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: The western Nian were pacified; he was memorialized for appointment as provincial commander or regional commander when a vacancy arose, and was advanced to Boqi Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: With the western Nian suppressed, he was recommended for the next provincial or regional commander vacancy and advanced to Boqi Baturu.

sentences.zh: 十年，署湖北提督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as acting provincial military commander of Hubei and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he served as acting provincial commander of Hubei and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，調湖南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 六年，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880 he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 近畿海防重要，奏令長樂駐蘆臺，扼大沽、北塘門戶。

translations.literal: Coastal defense near the capital was important; it was memorialized that Changle should be stationed at Lutai to hold the gateways of Dagu and Beitang.
translations.idiomatic: Because coastal defense near the capital mattered greatly, the court ordered Changle to Lutai to guard the approaches to Dagu and Beitang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒官，優恤，諡勤勇。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died in office; generous condolence was granted, and the posthumous title Qinyong was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1889; the court granted generous mourning honors and the posthumous name Qinyong ("Diligent and Brave").

sentences.zh: 楊鼎勳，字少銘，四川華陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Dingxun, courtesy name Shaoming, was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dingxun, styled Shaoming, came from Huayang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，應募從軍，初隸湖北按察使李孟群，克漢陽，擢把總。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he answered the recruitment and joined the army, first attached to Hubei surveillance commissioner Li Mengqun; Hanyang was captured and he was promoted to dartai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he enlisted, first under Hubei surveillance commissioner Li Mengqun; when Hanyang fell he was promoted to dartai.

sentences.zh: 七年，隸提督鮑超軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was attached to provincial military commander Bao Chao's army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he joined provincial commander Bao Chao's army.

sentences.zh: 八年，戰湖口，擢千總。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he fought at Hukou and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he fought at Hukou and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 十年，鮑超與陳玉成大戰小池驛，鼎勳見玉成立陣中指揮，獨從壯士十數人突前擊之，玉成駭走，复太湖、潛山兩城。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Bao Chao fought a great battle with Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi Post; Dingxun saw Yucheng standing in the formation directing; alone he followed a dozen stalwarts in a sudden forward attack; Yucheng fled in alarm; Taihu and Qianshan were both recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Bao Chao fought Chen Yucheng at Xiaochi Post; Dingxun saw Yucheng directing from within the enemy line and led a dozen picked men in a headlong charge that sent Yucheng fleeing and recovered Taihu and Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 敘功，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded and the peacock feather was granted.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was awarded the peacock-feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 李秀成踞黟縣，鼎勳擊賊城下，奪門入，大軍繼之，復其城。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng held Yi County; Dingxun attacked the rebels below the city wall, seized the gate and entered; the main army followed, and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiucheng held Yi County, Dingxun stormed the walls, forced a gate, and led the main force in to retake the city.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復建德，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Jiande was recovered and he was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he helped recover Jiande and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 破安慶赤岡嶺賊壘，擢游擊。

translations.literal: The rebel fort at Chigangling near Anqing was broken and he was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the rebel fort at Chigangling near Anqing and was made battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 初，小池驛之戰，鮑超嘉其功，令將五百人，所向有功。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the battle of Xiaochi Post, Bao Chao praised his merit and ordered him to command five hundred men; wherever he went there was achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After the fight at Xiaochi Post, Bao Chao praised his performance and gave him five hundred men, with whom he won success wherever he was sent.

sentences.zh: 諸將嫉之，譖於超。

translations.literal: The other generals were jealous of him and slandered him to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Other commanders grew jealous and slandered him to Bao Chao.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章督師上海，遂去超從淮軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang directed operations at Shanghai; he then left Chao and joined the Huai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, when Li Hongzhang took command at Shanghai, he left Bao Chao and joined the Huai Army.

sentences.zh: 虹橋、四江口諸戰有功，累擢副將。

translations.literal: At Hongqiao, Sijiangkou, and other battles he had merit and was repeatedly promoted to deputy regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at Hongqiao, Sijiangkou, and other engagements and was steadily promoted to deputy regional commander.

sentences.zh: 募淮勇千人，號勳字軍，屯金山張堰，扼平湖乍浦要衝，習西洋槍隊，每戰輒為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He recruited one thousand Huai braves called the Xunzi Army, encamped at Zhangyan in Jinshan to hold the vital passage of Pinghu and Zhabu, trained in Western musket companies, and in every battle was the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a thousand Huai braves as the Xunzi Army, held Zhangyan in Jinshan to block the Pinghu–Zhabu corridor, drilled them in Western musketry, and led the van in every fight.

sentences.zh: 二年，破新昌賊壘，連克楓涇，斬賊四千，生擒五百；

translations.literal: In the second year the rebel fort at Xinchang was broken, Fengjing was taken in succession, four thousand rebels were beheaded, and five hundred captured alive;
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he smashed the rebel fort at Xinchang, took Fengjing in succession, killed four thousand rebels, and captured five hundred alive;

sentences.zh: 再戰西塘，裹創奮擊，大敗之，擢總兵，賜號鋒勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: fighting again at Xitang, wrapping his wounds he charged fiercely and greatly defeated them; he was promoted to regional commander and granted the title Fengyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: then fought again at Xitang, bound his wounds, and charged until the enemy broke; he was made regional commander and given the title Fengyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 從程學啟規蘇州，鼎勳攻下城外堅壘，蘇州复，加提督銜。

translations.literal: Following Cheng Xueqi in planning for Suzhou, Dingxun stormed the strong outer fortifications; Suzhou was recovered and he was given brevet provincial commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Cheng Xueqi's campaign against Suzhou, took the outer fortifications, and when Suzhou fell received brevet provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，會克宜興、荊溪、溧陽，解常熟、無錫圍。

translations.literal: In the third year he jointly captured Yixing, Jingxi, and Liyang and lifted the sieges of Changshu and Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he helped take Yixing, Jingxi, and Liyang and lift the sieges of Changshu and Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 攻常州，賊因蘇州之殺降，惟死守。

translations.literal: Attacking Changzhou, because of the killing of those who surrendered at Suzhou the rebels would only defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzhou the rebels, remembering the massacre of surrendering troops at Suzhou, fought only to the death.

sentences.zh: 鼎勳以蜀人將淮勇，懼諸將輕己，每戰輒先，晝夜環攻，盡毀城外賊壘，血戰三日。

translations.literal: Dingxun, as a man of Shu commanding Huai braves, feared the other generals would look down on him; in every battle he was first; day and night he besieged in a ring, destroyed all rebel fortifications outside the walls, and fought bloody battles for three days.
translations.idiomatic: A Sichuanese leading Huai troops, Dingxun feared his peers would despise him, so he always led the assault, besieged day and night, destroyed every outer fort, and fought three days of bloody combat.

sentences.zh: 造浮橋，率死士先登城，砲彈洞胸達背，左右扶之，絕而復蘇，遂克常州，以提督記名簡放。

translations.literal: He built a pontoon bridge, led death-defying soldiers first to scale the wall; a cannonball pierced his chest through to his back; those at his sides supported him; he lost consciousness then revived; Changzhou was thus captured; he was recorded and selected for appointment as provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: He threw a pontoon bridge across the moat and led picked men up the wall first; a round passed through his chest and out his back, and his aides caught him as he collapsed, but he came to and Changzhou fell; he was entered on the rolls for provincial commander appointment.

sentences.zh: 創愈，進克浦口，复長興，招降湖州賊黨，會克其城。

translations.literal: When his wounds healed he advanced and captured Pukou, recovered Changxing, induced the surrender of rebel partisans in Huzhou, and jointly captured that city.
translations.idiomatic: Once healed, he took Pukou, recovered Changxing, induced Huzhou rebels to surrender, and helped capture the city.

sentences.zh: 追賊至皖境，克廣德。

translations.literal: Pursuing rebels into Anhui territory, he captured Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the enemy into Anhui, he took Guangde.

sentences.zh: 四年，偕郭松林援福建，攻烏頭門賊壘，复漳州，授江蘇蘇松鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went with Guo Songlin to relieve Fujian, attacked the rebel fort at Wutoumen, recovered Zhangzhou, and was appointed regional commander of Susong Town in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he sailed with Guo Songlin to Fujian, stormed the fort at Wutoumen, retook Zhangzhou, and was made regional commander of Susong in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 五年，調赴河南剿捻匪，敗賊硃仙鎮，躡擊至定陶、睢寧。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Henan to suppress Nian bandits, defeated rebels at Zhuxian Town, and pursued to Dingtao and Suining.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he was sent to Henan against the Nian, defeated them at Zhuxian Town, and pursued them to Dingtao and Suining.

sentences.zh: 六年，破賊於黃陂、孝感，擢浙江提督，調湖南。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he defeated rebels at Huangpi and Xiaogan, was promoted to provincial commander of Zhejiang, and transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he defeated bandits at Huangpi and Xiaogan, was made provincial commander of Zhejiang, and transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十月，破賊於山東濰縣，追至​​夏灣，賊酋陳懷忠乞降，分軍出周家寨襲賊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he defeated rebels at Weixian in Shandong, pursued to Xiawan; the rebel chief Chen Huaizhong begged to surrender; he divided his army to sally from Zhoujiazhai and strike the rebels, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In October he routed the bandits at Weixian in Shandong and pursued them to Xiawan; when the chief Chen Huaizhong offered to surrender, Dingxun sent a detachment from Zhoujiazhai to strike the main body and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 追擊於諸城、膠州。

translations.literal: Pursuit continued through Zhucheng and Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried through Zhucheng and Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，論功，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified, merit was assessed and he was given the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were suppressed, he received a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry title for his service.

sentences.zh: 七年，馳援畿輔，破捻匪於安平，追至楊家村，降賊酋張志清。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he rushed to relieve the capital region, broke Nian bandits at Anping, pursued to Yangjia Village, and induced the surrender of the rebel chief Zhang Zhiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he hurried to the capital districts, defeated the Nian at Anping, pursued them to Yangjia Village, and accepted the surrender of the bandit chief Zhang Zhiqing.

sentences.zh: 偕郭松林擊賊濬縣大邳山，又敗之衛輝，陣斬賊酋王建瀛、熊八，擒悍賊何士喜、周久於龍王廟。

translations.literal: Together with Guo Songlin he struck rebels at Dapishan in Jun County, again defeated them at Weihui, killed in battle the rebel chiefs Wang Jianying and Xiong Ba, and captured the fierce rebels He Shixi and Zhou Jiu at Longwang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: With Guo Songlin he fought at Dapishan in Jun County and again at Weihui, killed the chiefs Wang Jianying and Xiong Ba in battle, and captured the fierce bandits He Shixi and Zhou Jiu at Longwang Temple.

sentences.zh: 賊竄山東，自德州趨天津，鼎勳守運河，修牆浚壕，賊來犯，輒擊走之。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into Shandong, from Dezhou toward Tianjin; Dingxun guarded the Grand Canal, repaired walls and deepened moats, and whenever rebels came to attack he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits slipped into Shandong and headed from Dezhou toward Tianjin, Dingxun held the Grand Canal line, strengthened walls and ditches, and beat back every attack.

sentences.zh: 會舊傷發，遽卒，數日而西捻平。

translations.literal: Just then his old wounds reopened and he died suddenly; within days the western Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His old wounds reopened and he died suddenly; the western Nian were suppressed a few days later.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏聞，贈太子少保，諡忠勤，建專祠。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized the throne; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Zhongqin, and a special shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang reported his death to the throne; the court posthumously made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave him the name Zhongqin, and built him a dedicated shrine.

sentences.zh: 唐殿魁，字藎臣，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Tang Diankui, courtesy name Jinchen, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Diankui, styled Jinchen, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，巡撫翁同書檄率鄉團援壽州，力解城圍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, by order of Governor Weng Tonghe he led local militia to relieve Shouzhou and strenuously lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, on orders from Governor Weng Tonghe, he led local militia to relieve Shouzhou and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 又從克合肥三河汛，解六安圍，敘千總。

translations.literal: He again followed in the capture of Sanhe Post at Hefei and lifted the siege of Lu'an; merit was recorded and he was made company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped take Sanhe Post at Hefei and lift the siege of Lu'an, and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章率淮軍援上海，殿魁從，隸劉銘傳，克南匯、川沙、奉賢、金山衛、柘林五城，積功累擢都司，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang led the Huai Army to relieve Shanghai; Diankui followed, was attached to Liu Mingchuan, captured the five cities of Nanhui, Chuansha, Fengxian, Jinshanwei, and Zhelin, and through accumulated merit was repeatedly promoted to battalion commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he joined Li Hongzhang's Huai Army at Shanghai under Liu Mingchuan, helped take Nanhui, Chuansha, Fengxian, Jinshanwei, and Zhelin, and rose to battalion commander with the peacock-feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 二年，克江陰楊舍汛城，擢游擊，賜號振勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the second year the garrison city of Yangshe in Jiangyin was captured; he was promoted to battalion commander and granted the title Zhenyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he took the Yangshe garrison in Jiangyin, was made battalion commander, and received the title Zhenyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 复江陰縣城，擢參將。

translations.literal: The Jiangyin county seat was recovered and he was promoted to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the Jiangyin county seat and was promoted to brigade general.

sentences.zh: 尋克無錫，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wuxi was captured and he was recorded with the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi fell soon after, and he was entered on the rolls as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 從劉銘傳攻常州，銘傳受重傷，令殿魁偕副將黃桂蘭督兵進。

translations.literal: Following Liu Mingchuan in the attack on Changzhou, Mingchuan was severely wounded and ordered Diankui together with deputy regional commander Huang Guilan to direct the troops forward.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Changzhou, when Mingchuan was badly wounded, he put Diankui and deputy commander Huang Guilan in charge of the advance.

sentences.zh: 甫至奔牛鎮，而常州、丹陽兩路賊麕至，圍之。

translations.literal: Just as he reached Benniu Town, rebels from both Changzhou and Danyang paths gathered and surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached Benniu when rebel columns from Changzhou and Danyang converged and surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 殿魁據石營依河岸，壁壘悉為賊轟毀，堅守二十餘日。

translations.literal: Diankui held a stone camp along the riverbank; all fortifications were smashed by rebel bombardment, yet he defended stubbornly for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Diankui held a stone camp on the riverbank; rebel fire demolished his works, but he held out for more than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 銘傳裹創往救，殿魁從內夾擊，苦戰數日，圍始解。

translations.literal: Mingchuan, wounds bound, went to relieve him; Diankui struck from within in a pincer; after bitter fighting for several days the siege was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan came with his wounds bound, Diankui attacked from inside, and after several days of hard fighting the encirclement was broken.

sentences.zh: 三年，克常州，生擒賊首陳坤書，以提督記名。

translations.literal: In the third year Changzhou was captured and the rebel chief Chen Kunshu was taken alive; he was recorded with the rank of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Changzhou fell and the rebel chief Chen Kunshu was captured alive; Diankui was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，增募所部至三千人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he increased recruitment of his command to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he expanded his command to three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 從劉銘傳渡淮剿捻匪，破張寨賊壘。

translations.literal: Following Liu Mingchuan he crossed the Huai to suppress Nian bandits and broke the rebel fort at Zhangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Huai with Liu Mingchuan against the Nian and stormed the fort at Zhangzhai.

sentences.zh: 五年，授浙江衢州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed regional commander of Quzhou Town in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he was appointed regional commander at Quzhou in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 追賊至湖北，克黃陂。

translations.literal: Pursuing rebels into Hubei, he captured Huangpi.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the bandits into Hubei, he took Huangpi.

sentences.zh: 捻匪自山東回竄，銘傳督兵追至烏官屯，殿魁繼進，殺賊五百餘。

translations.literal: Nian bandits fled back from Shandong; Mingchuan directed troops in pursuit to Wuguantun; Diankui followed and killed more than five hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian doubled back from Shandong, Mingchuan pursued them to Wuguantun and Diankui followed up, killing more than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 六年，調廣西右江鎮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Youjiang Town in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was transferred to Youjiang in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 捻首張總愚竄安陸。

translations.literal: The Nian chief Zhang Zongyu fled into Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian chief Zhang Zongyu fled into Anlu.

sentences.zh: 銘傳與鮑超約會戰於永漋河，銘傳欲先出，殿魁請少待，不從。

translations.literal: Mingchuan and Bao Chao agreed to join battle at the Yongzhang River; Mingchuan wished to advance first; Diankui asked him to wait briefly, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan and Bao Chao had agreed to meet the enemy at the Yongzhang River; Mingchuan wanted to attack first, and though Diankui urged him to wait, he refused.

sentences.zh: 超未至，銘軍先遇賊，部將田履安、李錫增戰沒。

translations.literal: Before Chao arrived, Ming's army met the rebels first; subordinate generals Tian Lü'an and Li Xizeng died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chao had not yet arrived when Mingchuan's force met the bandits; generals Tian Lü'an and Li Xizeng were killed.

sentences.zh: 殿魁戰小挫，受重傷。

translations.literal: Diankui suffered a small setback in battle and received severe wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Diankui's column was driven back and he was badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 及聞霆軍大捷，复裹創力戰，遂殞於陣。

translations.literal: When he heard of the Thunder Army's great victory, again binding his wounds he fought hard and thus fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: When word came of Bao Chao's great victory, he bound his wounds and fought on until he was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡忠壯，建專祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Captain, the posthumous title Zhongzhuang, and a special shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted hereditary Commandant of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Captain titles, gave him the name Zhongzhuang, and built a dedicated shrine.

sentences.zh: 唐定奎，字俊侯，殿魁弟。

translations.literal: Tang Dingkui, courtesy name Junhou, was Diankui's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Dingkui, styled Junhou, was Diankui's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 偕兄轉戰江蘇。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother he campaigned across Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought alongside his brother across Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 從劉銘傳剿捻於山東、河南、安徽、湖北，積功累擢副將，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Following Liu Mingchuan he suppressed Nian bandits in Shandong, Henan, Anhui, and Hubei; through accumulated merit he was repeatedly promoted to deputy regional commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Mingchuan he fought the Nian in Shandong, Henan, Anhui, and Hubei, rose to deputy regional commander, and received the peacock-feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，殿魁戰歿永漋河，定奎方省母回裡，奔赴軍，誓殺賊復仇，遂代領兄舊部，轉戰河南、山東。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi Diankui died in battle at the Yongzhang River; Dingkui was just visiting his mother at home, rushed to the army, swore to kill rebels and avenge his brother, and thus took command of his brother's old troops, campaigning in Henan and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 Diankui was killed at the Yongzhang River; Dingkui was home visiting his mother, hurried back to camp, swore to avenge his brother, took over the old command, and fought on in Henan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 六年，殄任柱於贛榆，破賴文光於壽光，所部殺賊最多。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Ren Zhu was destroyed at Ganyu and Lai Wenguang was broken at Shouguang; his unit killed the most rebels.
translations.idiomatic: That year his troops helped destroy Ren Zhu at Ganyu and break Lai Wenguang at Shouguang, and his unit accounted for more kills than any other.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，以提督記名。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified he was recorded with the rank of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were suppressed, he was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，從剿西捻於直隸、山東，賜號呼敦巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in suppressing the western Nian in Zhili and Shandong and was granted the title Hudun Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he joined the campaign against the western Nian in Zhili and Shandong and received the title Hudun Baturu.

sentences.zh: 銘軍凱旋，告歸終養。

translations.literal: When Ming's army returned in triumph he requested leave to go home and care for his parents in their old age.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingchuan's army returned victorious, he asked to go home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 九年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 劉銘傳赴陝西剿回匪，調定奎接統銘武軍，定奎請終制，命俟陝西軍事平，回籍終制。

translations.literal: Liu Mingchuan went to Shaanxi to suppress Muslim rebels; Dingkui was transferred to take over the Mingwu Army; Dingkui requested to complete mourning; he was ordered to wait until Shaanxi military affairs were settled, then return home to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Mingchuan went to Shaanxi against Muslim rebels, Dingkui was ordered to take the Mingwu Army; he asked to finish mourning first and was told to wait until the Shaanxi campaign ended, then return home.

sentences.zh: 十年，定奎回防徐州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Dingkui returned to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he returned to garrison Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，日本擾台灣，生番滋事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Japan harassed Taiwan and aboriginal tribes caused disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: In 1874 Japan raided Taiwan and indigenous tribes rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 船政大臣沈葆楨奏請援師，李鴻章薦定奎率所部往。

translations.literal: Naval affairs minister Shen Baozhen memorialized requesting relief troops; Li Hongzhang recommended Dingkui to lead his command there.
translations.idiomatic: Naval minister Shen Baozhen asked for reinforcements, and Li Hongzhang recommended Dingkui to lead his troops to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 七月，至台灣，駐鳳山，擇險分屯。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he reached Taiwan, encamped at Fengshan, and chose defensible points to divide his garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In July he landed in Taiwan, based himself at Fengshan, and posted troops at key strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 龜紋番社引日兵與刺桐腳莊民尋仇相閧，定奎示以兵威，日人引去。

translations.literal: The Guiwen aboriginal community led Japanese troops and villagers of Citongjiao in mutual vendetta fighting; Dingkui displayed military might and the Japanese withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guiwen tribe drew Japanese troops into a feud with villagers at Citongjiao, Dingkui showed force and the Japanese pulled back.

sentences.zh: 時疫流行，士卒先後死千餘人，定奎拊循周至，兵氣不衰，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Epidemic disease was widespread; more than a thousand soldiers died in succession; Dingkui comforted and cared for them thoroughly; army morale did not decline; the yellow riding jacket was granted.
translations.idiomatic: An epidemic killed more than a thousand of his men, but Dingkui nursed the troops so carefully that morale held, and he received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 楓港、獅頭諸社番屢出戕害良民，光緒元年，游擊王開俊進剿，中伏死。

translations.literal: Aboriginal communities at Fenggang, Shitou, and elsewhere repeatedly came out to kill peaceful subjects; in the first year of Guangxu battalion commander Wang Kaijun advanced to suppress them and died in an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Aboriginal bands around Fenggang and Shitou kept killing civilians; in 1875 battalion commander Wang Kaijun led a punitive expedition and was killed in an ambush.

sentences.zh: 內外番社結黨劫殺，各社就撫，皆懷觀望。

translations.literal: Interior and exterior aboriginal communities formed factions to rob and kill; each community that came to submit still harbored watchful hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Interior and coastal tribes formed raiding bands; even those who came in to submit remained wary and undecided.

sentences.zh: 定奎分遣七營屯東港南勢湖，自率四營當其衝，葆楨檄諸軍並聽節制。

translations.literal: Dingkui dispatched seven battalions to garrison Donggang and Nanshihu, personally led four battalions to meet the main thrust, and Baozhen ordered all armies alike to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: Dingkui posted seven battalions at Donggang and Nanshihu, kept four under his own command on the main axis, and Baozhen placed all forces under his orders.

sentences.zh: 定奎上書陳兵事，略曰：「逆番晝伏莽中，夜燎山頂，精於標槍，伺間輒發。

translations.literal: Dingkui submitted a memorial on military affairs, stating in summary: "The rebellious tribes hide by day in the thickets, at night light beacon fires on the hilltops, are skilled with throwing spears, and strike whenever they see an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Dingkui wrote to the court on the campaign, saying in part: "The hostile tribes hide in the brush by day, signal from the hilltops at night, are expert with javelins, and attack at every chance.

sentences.zh: 專恃深林密箐，狙擊我師，我進彼隱，我退彼見。

translations.literal: They rely solely on deep forests and dense ravines to snipe at our army: when we advance they hide, when we withdraw they appear.
translations.idiomatic: They depend on deep forest and narrow ravines to ambush our columns: when we advance they vanish, when we pull back they show themselves.

sentences.zh: 今欲掃其巢穴，必先翦其荊棘。

translations.literal: If we now wish to sweep away their nests, we must first cut away their thorns and brambles.
translations.idiomatic: To destroy their strongholds we must first clear the jungle that shelters them.

sentences.zh: 宜增募土勇，導引兵丁，隨山刊木，務絕根株，然後分道進兵，草薙擒狝。

translations.literal: We should recruit more local braves to guide the soldiers, cut trees as we follow the mountains, strive to uproot them entirely, then advance in separate columns and mow them down like grass.
translations.idiomatic: We should raise more local scouts to guide the troops, cut the forest as we advance along the ridges, root them out completely, then attack in separate columns and cut them down.

sentences.zh: 其有奸民接濟鹽米火藥者，按軍法，庶幾一舉可以成功。

translations.literal: Those treacherous subjects who supply them salt, rice, and gunpowder should be dealt with by military law; then perhaps in one effort success may be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Traitors who supply them salt, grain, and gunpowder must be punished under military law; only then can we hope to succeed in one campaign."

sentences.zh: 」葆楨據以入告。

translations.literal: Baozhen forwarded this memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen forwarded the memorial to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 於是開山進兵，攻克萃山、竹坑、本武諸社。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened mountain paths and advanced, capturing the communities of Cuishan, Zhukeng, Benwu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut roads into the mountains and took the communities of Cuishan, Zhukeng, Benwu, and others.

sentences.zh: 獅頭社猶負險抗拒，定奎令諸將得險即守，自剿獅頭兩社，別遣師扼斷外援，遂攻下之。

translations.literal: The Shitou communities still relied on difficult terrain to resist; Dingkui ordered the generals to hold any strong point they gained; he personally suppressed the two Shitou communities while sending another force to cut off outside aid, and thus stormed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Shitou tribes still held the high ground; Dingkui told his officers to secure every advantage gained, led the assault on the two Shitou communities himself, sent another column to block outside help, and took them.

sentences.zh: 移營駐守，被脅十餘社皆歸命，給衣履酒食，譯示朝廷威德，咸受約束。

translations.literal: He shifted camp to garrison the area; more than ten communities that had been coerced all submitted; he gave them clothing, shoes, food, and wine, had interpreters explain the court's majesty and virtue, and all accepted restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He moved camp to hold the region; more than ten coerced communities submitted; he gave them clothes, food, and wine, had interpreters explain imperial authority, and brought them all under control.

sentences.zh: 設招撫局，示約七條，曰：遵薙發，編戶口，獻凶逆，禁仇殺，立總目，墾番地，設番塾。

translations.literal: He established a pacification bureau and proclaimed seven articles of agreement: observe the shaving of the forelock, register households, surrender criminals, forbid vendetta killing, appoint headmen, open aboriginal land to cultivation, and set up aboriginal schools.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a pacification office and announced seven rules: adopt Qing hairstyle, register households, hand over criminals, end blood feuds, appoint headmen, open tribal land to farming, and establish tribal schools.

sentences.zh: 以龜紋番酋充諸社總目，赦其脅從。

translations.literal: He appointed the Guiwen aboriginal chief as headman over the various communities and pardoned those who had been coerced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: He made the Guiwen chief headman over the communities and pardoned those who had been forced to join the revolt.

sentences.zh: 台南大定，詔褒獎，命內渡休養士卒。

translations.literal: Southern Taiwan was greatly pacified; an edict praised and rewarded him and ordered him to cross to the mainland to rest his troops.
translations.idiomatic: With southern Taiwan pacified, the court praised his service and ordered him to bring his troops back to the mainland to recuperate.

sentences.zh: 授直隸正定鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed regional commander of Zhengding Town in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regional commander at Zhengding in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 尋擢福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to provincial commander of Fujian land forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to provincial commander of Fujian's land forces.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨調兩江總督，奏統所部駐防江陰。

translations.literal: When Shen Baozhen was transferred to governor-general of Liangjiang, he memorialized that Dingkui should command his troops in garrison at Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Baozhen became governor-general of Liangjiang, he had Dingkui's troops stationed at Jiangyin under his command.

sentences.zh: 九年，傷發乞休，不允。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his wounds reopened and he begged to retire; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 his old wounds flared and he asked to retire, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 法越用兵事起，海防戒嚴，詔促力疾赴防。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese war began, coastal defense was placed on alert; an edict urged him to exert himself despite illness and hurry to defense posts.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between France and Vietnam, coastal defenses were mobilized and he was ordered to take up his post despite illness.

sentences.zh: 十一年，和議定，病請開缺，允之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year peace was concluded; he pleaded illness to vacate his post and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 peace was made; he resigned on grounds of illness and was allowed to step down.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，優恤，諡果介。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died; generous condolence was granted and the posthumous title Guojie was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1887; the court granted generous mourning honors and the posthumous name Guojie.

sentences.zh: 滕嗣武，湖南麻陽人。

translations.literal: Teng Siwu was a native of Mayang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Siwu came from Mayang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從軍湖北。

translations.literal: In the early Xianfeng period he joined the army in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng era he enlisted in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十年，小池驛之戰，功多，超擢都司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, at the battle of Xiaochi Post, his merit was great and he was exceptionally promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, at Xiaochi Post, his merit earned him an exceptional promotion to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 從攻安慶，嗣武率所部扼要築砲壘，壘未成，賊突出萬餘來爭，嗣武力擊破之。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Anqing, Siwu led his unit to hold a vital point and build gun emplacements; before the emplacements were finished more than ten thousand rebels sallied forth to contest them; Siwu struck hard and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Anqing he seized a key point to build batteries; before they were finished more than ten thousand rebels rushed out to take them, and Siwu beat them back.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，敘功擢參將。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was captured; merit was recorded and he was promoted to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: When Anqing fell in 1861 he was promoted to brigade general for his service.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，改隸淮軍，從李鴻章至上海，解松江圍，賜號偉勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was transferred to the Huai Army, followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, lifted the siege of Songjiang, and was granted the title Weiyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he joined the Huai Army, followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, lifted the siege of Songjiang, and received the title Weiyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 屯北簳山扼賊衝，賊犯寶山，與諸軍夾擊破之，進拔南匯，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He encamped at Beigan Mountain to block the rebel thrust; when rebels attacked Baoshan he joined other armies in a pincer and broke them, advanced and took Nanhui, and was recorded with the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He held Beigan Mountain to block the enemy line; when rebels struck Baoshan he helped rout them in a pincer, took Nanhui, and was entered on the rolls as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 二年，偕程學啟規蘇州，敗賊於正義鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year he joined Cheng Xueqi in planning for Suzhou and defeated rebels at Zhengyi Town.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he joined Cheng Xueqi's campaign against Suzhou and defeated the rebels at Zhengyi Town.

sentences.zh: 地當要衝，以嗣武守之，輔以水師，分軍伏橋口伺賊。

translations.literal: The place was a vital passage; Siwu was assigned to hold it, supported by the naval force, with part of the army ambushed at the bridge mouth to watch for rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The position was strategically vital; Siwu held it with naval support while a detachment lay in ambush at the bridge.

sentences.zh: 崑山賊勢蹙，啟西門遁。

translations.literal: Rebel strength at Kunshan was pressed; they opened the west gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed at Kunshan, the rebels opened the west gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 伏起，水師以巨砲環擊，賊大潰，立復其城。

translations.literal: The ambush rose; the naval force bombarded them with great cannon in a ring; the rebels fled in great rout and the city was immediately recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush sprang up, the fleet shelled them with heavy guns, the enemy broke completely, and Kunshan was retaken at once.

sentences.zh: 移軍會攻江陰。

translations.literal: He shifted his army to join in the attack on Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his troops to join the assault on Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 賊自無錫來援，連營數十，柵壘棋布。

translations.literal: Rebels came from Wuxi to relieve the city; they linked camps by the dozens and spread palisades and fortifications like chess pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces came from Wuxi, pitching dozens of linked camps with fortifications spread across the ground like chessmen.

sentences.zh: 軍分三路進，嗣武率八營當中路，攻​​麥市橋，以輕兵伏河堤，燃砲毀賊壘，賊潰走，追及之三巴橋，殲獲殆盡。

translations.literal: The army advanced in three columns; Siwu led eight battalions on the center route, attacked Maishi Bridge, placed light troops in ambush on the river embankment, fired heated shot to destroy rebel fortifications, the rebels fled in rout, pursuit reached Sanba Bridge, and they were nearly all destroyed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced in three columns; Siwu led eight battalions up the center against Maishi Bridge, hid light troops along the embankment, burned out the rebel works with heated shot, routed the enemy, pursued them to Sanba Bridge, and killed or captured nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 進次無錫城下，賊首李世賢以全軍拒戰。

translations.literal: Advancing he halted below Wuxi city; the rebel chief Li Shixian met him with his full army.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and camped below Wuxi, where the rebel chief Li Shixian met him with his entire force.

sentences.zh: 嗣武身先士卒，怒馬突陣，敗之謝家橋，又敗之蕩口。

translations.literal: Siwu was first among the soldiers, charging the line on a spirited horse; he defeated them at Xiejia Bridge and again at Dangkou.
translations.idiomatic: Siwu led from the front, charging on a fiery horse, and routed them at Xiejia Bridge and again at Dangkou.

sentences.zh: 賊退據硃王橋堅守，嗣武出奇兵襲擊，擒斬千餘，加提督銜。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated and held Zhuwang Bridge stubbornly; Siwu sent surprise troops in a raid, capturing and beheading more than a thousand, and was given brevet provincial commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to hold Zhuwang Bridge; Siwu sent a surprise column, killed or captured more than a thousand, and received brevet provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 既而克無錫，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wuxi was captured and he was recorded with the rank of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi fell soon after, and he was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，會攻常州，破援賊於奔牛鎮，攻下宜興、荊溪，嗣武傷右股。

translations.literal: In the third year he joined in the attack on Changzhou, broke relieving rebels at Benniu Town, stormed Yixing and Jingxi, and Siwu was wounded in the right thigh.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he joined the assault on Changzhou, routed relief forces at Benniu, took Yixing and Jingxi, and was wounded in the right thigh.

sentences.zh: 四月，會圍常州，嗣武當南門，砲毀城垣，克之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the encirclement of Changzhou closed; Siwu held the south gate; cannon destroyed the wall; the city was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In April, as Changzhou was encircled, Siwu held the south gate, artillery breached the wall, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 七年，從李鴻章剿捻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Li Hongzhang in suppressing the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he joined Li Hongzhang's campaign against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 畿輔事平。

translations.literal: Affairs in the capital region were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting around the capital was brought to an end.

sentences.zh: 八年，授湖北鄖陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed regional commander of Yunyang Town in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he was appointed regional commander at Yunyang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，賜卹，諡武慎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; condolence gifts were granted and the posthumous title Wushen was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1872; the court granted mourning honors and the posthumous name Wushen.

sentences.zh: 駱國忠，安徽鳳陽人。

translations.literal: Luo Guozhong was a native of Fengyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guozhong came from Fengyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初陷於粵匪，授偽職，知賊必敗，陰圖反正。

translations.literal: At first he was trapped among the Guangdong rebels and given a false office; knowing the rebels would certainly be defeated, he secretly plotted to return to the right side.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been caught up with the Taiping rebels and given a false rank, but seeing they were doomed, he secretly planned to defect.

sentences.zh: 常熟久為賊踞，福山與狼山夾江對峙，賊設屯以扼後路，國忠任城守。

translations.literal: Changshu had long been held by rebels; Fushan and Langshan faced each other across the river; rebels set garrisons to choke the rear route; Guozhong was charged with defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Changshu had long been in rebel hands; Fushan and Langshan faced each other across the river, and the rebels posted garrisons to block the rear; Guozhong was put in charge of the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章蒞江蘇，兵威日振，國忠因水師游擊周興隆舉城薙發降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang arrived in Jiangsu and military prestige daily strengthened; through naval battalion commander Zhou Xinglong, Guozhong surrendered the city with the shaving of the forelock.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, as Li Hongzhang's power in Jiangsu grew, Guozhong surrendered the city through naval commander Zhou Xinglong, adopting the Qing hairstyle as a sign of submission.

sentences.zh: 鴻章令興隆、國忠選驍健萬人，分守水陸要衝，以防蘇州竄賊。

translations.literal: Hongzhang ordered Xinglong and Guozhong to select ten thousand stalwart men and divide them to guard vital passages by land and water against rebels fleeing from Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang had them pick ten thousand tough fighters to hold key points on land and water against rebels slipping out of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 福山守賊胡經元、江勝海原約俱降，國忠遣人召之，比至福山，不得入。

translations.literal: The Fushan garrison rebels Hu Jingyuan and Jiang Shenghai had originally agreed to surrender together; Guozhong sent men to summon them, but by the time they reached Fushan they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Fushan garrison commanders Hu Jingyuan and Jiang Shenghai had agreed to surrender, but when Guozhong summoned them to Fushan they could not get in.

sentences.zh: 國忠夜率兵往，令其弟國孝攻其南，自與興隆攻其北，斷賊登舟之路，槍殪賊將侯得龍，賊舟師遁走。

translations.literal: Guozhong led troops by night; he ordered his younger brother Guoxiao to attack from the south while he himself with Xinglong attacked from the north, cut off the rebels' path to their boats, shot dead the rebel general Hou Delong, and the rebel naval force fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong marched by night, sent his brother Guoxiao against the south while he and Xinglong attacked from the north, cut off access to the boats, killed the rebel commander Hou Delong, and drove off the rebel fleet.

sentences.zh: 經元、勝海殺賊渠數人，率所部出，與國忠合。

translations.literal: Jingyuan and Shenghai killed several rebel ringleaders, led their units out, and joined Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan and Shenghai killed several rebel leaders, brought their men out, and joined Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 國孝越重壕毀賊壘；

translations.literal: Guoxiao crossed deep moats and destroyed rebel fortifications;
translations.idiomatic: Guoxiao crossed the deep moats and smashed the rebel works;

sentences.zh: 興隆等分兵盡拔許浦、白茅、徐涇諸壘，賊將錢壽仁亦自太倉率所部二千詣鴻章降。

translations.literal: Xinglong and others divided forces and captured all the forts at Xupu, Baimao, and Xujing; the rebel general Qian Shouren also came from Taicang with two thousand of his men to surrender to Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xinglong's columns took the forts at Xupu, Baimao, and Xujing, and rebel general Qian Shouren came from Taicang with two thousand men to surrender to Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 總兵鞠耀乾率師船泊徐涇，千總袁光政入城助守。

translations.literal: Regional commander Ju Yaoqian led armed ships to anchor at Xujing; company commander Yuan Guangzheng entered the city to help defend.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Ju Yaoqian brought gunboats to Xujing, and company commander Yuan Guangzheng entered the city to reinforce the defense.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李秀成等以眾數万自蘇州來攻，連營十餘裡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Li Xiucheng and others came from Suzhou to attack with a force of tens of thousands, linking camps for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: In December Li Xiucheng marched from Suzhou with tens of thousands of men and pitched a camp line more than ten li long.

sentences.zh: 國忠乞濟師，常勝軍五百人自海道往援，而賊由江陰再陷福山，聲援隔絕。

translations.literal: Guozhong begged for relieving troops; five hundred men of the Ever-Victorious Army came by sea to aid, but rebels from Jiangyin again captured Fushan and support was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong asked for reinforcements; five hundred Ever-Victorious Army men came by sea, but rebels from Jiangyin retook Fushan and cut him off from help.
