sentences.zh: 鴻章令潘鼎新、劉銘傳、張樹珊以三千人趨福山，與黃翼升水師並進。

translations.literal: Hongzhang ordered Pan Dingxin, Liu Mingchuan, and Zhang Shushan to hurry to Fushan with three thousand men, advancing together with Huang Yisheng's naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang sent Pan Dingxin, Liu Mingchuan, and Zhang Shushan with three thousand men toward Fushan, supported by Huang Yisheng's fleet.

sentences.zh: 福山城小而堅，攻之不下。

translations.literal: Fushan city was small but strong and could not be taken by assault.
translations.idiomatic: Fushan was small but stout and resisted assault.

sentences.zh: 常熟被圍愈亟，國忠斂兵入城，興隆屯城西虞山相犄角，為死守計。

translations.literal: The siege of Changshu grew more pressing; Guozhong drew his troops into the city; Xinglong encamped on Yushan west of the city in mutual support, planning to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege of Changshu tightened, Guozhong pulled his men inside the walls while Xinglong held Yushan west of the city in mutual support, preparing to fight to the last.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊以砲壞城東垣，國忠力拒不得入，樹雲梯緣城，亦擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the second year rebels used cannon to breach the eastern wall; Guozhong fought hard and kept them from entering; they raised scaling ladders along the wall and he beat them back as well.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 rebel artillery smashed the eastern wall, but Guozhong held them out; when they raised scaling ladders along the ramparts, he drove them back again.

sentences.zh: 賊增壘掘隧，數道並進，城危甚。

translations.literal: The rebels added fortifications and dug tunnels, advancing on several routes at once; the city was in grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels built more works and dug tunnels, pressing the attack on several fronts, and the city was in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 會鼎新、銘傳諸軍急攻福山，賊分兵赴援，留者僅數千，國忠乃開城出戰，毀賊壘，擒其渠硃衣點。

translations.literal: Just then Dingxin, Mingchuan, and the other armies pressed the attack on Fushan; the rebels divided forces to relieve it, leaving only a few thousand; Guozhong then opened the city and sallied forth, destroyed rebel fortifications, and captured their ringleader Zhuyi Dian.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingxin and Mingchuan stormed Fushan, the rebels sent most of their force to relieve it, leaving only a few thousand; Guozhong sallied out, destroyed their works, and captured the ringleader Zhuyi Dian.

sentences.zh: 福山既克，諸軍來會，城圍始解。

translations.literal: Once Fushan was captured the armies came together and the siege of the city was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: After Fushan fell the relieving armies arrived and the siege was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，優詔嘉獎，擢授國忠副將，加總兵銜，編降眾為忠字八營。

translations.literal: When victory was reported an edict graciously praised and rewarded him; Guozhong was promoted to deputy regional commander with brevet regional commander rank, and the surrendered troops were organized into eight battalions under the name Zhongzi.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought an imperial commendation; Guozhong was made deputy regional commander with brevet regional commander rank, and his surrendered troops were organized into eight Zhongzi battalions.

sentences.zh: 會攻江陰，戰甚力，既克，賜號勁勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He joined in the attack on Jiangyin and fought with great force; after it was captured he was granted the title Jinyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hard in the assault on Jiangyin and, after its fall, received the title Jinyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 署京口水師副將，留守江陰。

translations.literal: He served as acting deputy commander of the Jingkou naval force and remained to garrison Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting deputy commander of the Jingkou naval force and stayed to garrison Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 三年，破丹陽援賊，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the third year he broke relieving rebels from Danyang and was recorded with the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he routed relief forces from Danyang and was entered on the rolls as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 尋克常州，以積勞傷發，乞假歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Changzhou was captured; because accumulated labor caused his wounds to reopen, he begged leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou fell soon after, but overwork reopened his old wounds and he went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 五年，從劉銘傳剿捻匪，轉戰湖北、河南、山東，所鄉有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Liu Mingchuan in suppressing Nian bandits, campaigning through Hubei, Henan, and Shandong; wherever he went there was merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he joined Liu Mingchuan against the Nian and fought across Hubei, Henan, and Shandong with steady success.

sentences.zh: 六年，東捻平，以提督記名，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the eastern Nian were pacified; he was recorded with the rank of provincial commander and granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Nian were suppressed in 1867, he was entered on the rolls as provincial commander and received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 九年，銘傳督辦陝西軍務，調國忠從行。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Mingchuan supervised military affairs in Shaanxi and Guozhong was transferred to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870, when Mingchuan took charge of operations in Shaanxi, Guozhong was ordered to go with him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒於乾州軍中，賜卹，諡勇肅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in the army at Qianzhou; condolence gifts were granted and the posthumous title Yongsu was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp at Qianzhou in 1873; the court granted mourning honors and the posthumous name Yongsu.

sentences.zh: 論曰：郭松林、李長樂、楊鼎勳、滕嗣武皆由湘、楚舊部改隸淮軍，平吳、平捻，卓著聲績。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, and Teng Siwu all came from old Xiang and Chu units and were transferred to the Huai Army; in pacifying Wu and pacifying the Nian their fame and achievement were outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Guo Songlin, Li Changle, Yang Dingxun, and Teng Siwu all transferred from old Xiang and Chu units into the Huai Army and won outstanding renown pacifying Jiangnan and suppressing the Nian.

sentences.zh: 唐殿魁淮軍驍將，惜未竟功。

translations.literal: Tang Diankui was a fierce general of the Huai Army; it is a pity he did not complete his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Diankui was a fierce Huai Army fighter who died before his full measure of achievement.

sentences.zh: 定奎席兄餘光，名位轉出其上，固有幸有不幸哉。

translations.literal: Dingkui rested on his elder brother's remaining glory, yet name and rank in the end rose above him—is this not a matter of fortune and misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Dingkui built on his brother's reputation yet surpassed him in rank and fame—was that fortune or misfortune?

sentences.zh: 駱國忠智勇堅毅，識時為傑，當時名滿江南，成績可紀也。

translations.literal: Luo Guozhong was intelligent, brave, and resolute, discerning the times as a hero; at the time his name filled Jiangnan, and his achievements are worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guozhong was intelligent, brave, and resolute, a man who read the times rightly; his name filled Jiangnan in his day, and his record stands as one worth preserving.
